observations: Photo shows two rectangular power-bank style casings on the floor.
Both units have visible wear/marks; one has a taped/covered area on the top surface.
There are multiple blue cables connected/lying around the units.
No brand name, model number, capacity (mAh), or label is readable in the photo.
No ports/LED indicators are clearly shown; no screen or charging indicator is visible.

claims.claim: Scrap power banks for sale in Ibadan.
claims.evidence: Only generic power-bank casings are visible; the photo does not confirm they are scrap/defective, and the location (Ibadan) is not verifiable from the image.

risks.risk: Whether the power banks actually work (capacity/charging output) vs. fully dead scrap.
risks.proof: A short video showing each unit charging a phone (plug in, show charging icon/percentage change) and/or showing output voltage/current on a USB tester.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / for parts only.

risks.risk: Battery safety risk (swollen, leaking, or damaged cells) that can make them unsafe to transport/use.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of both units from all sides showing any swelling, dents, leakage, or burnt smell confirmation; plus a photo of the battery compartment if accessible.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unsafe/for scrap only (lowest value).

risks.risk: Unknown capacity (mAh) and quality (cell type), which heavily affects value.
risks.proof: Photo of the label/sticker showing capacity (mAh), input/output ratings (e.g., 5V/2A, 9V/2A), and brand/model—on each unit.

risks.risk: Cables/ports may be mismatched or damaged; the units may not charge due to port/cable issues rather than the battery.
risks.proof: Photo of the USB ports (close-up) and a test using a known-good cable for each unit.

proof_requests: Send close-up photos of each unit’s label/sticker (capacity mAh and input/output ratings).
Send a video test: plug each power bank into a phone and show the phone charging (percentage increases).
Show a USB power meter/USB tester reading for output (voltage/current) for each unit.
Show close-ups of the casing for swelling/leakage/burn marks and confirm whether any unit is physically damaged.
response.reason: From the single photo, the items look like worn power-bank casings, but there’s no readable capacity/brand and no proof they work or are safe. Without a charging/output test and label details, a reliable worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
